question.text: Magadha Capital Cat II AIF switches its investee company's valuation methodology from DCF to EV/EBITDA multiples. Per SEBI framework, this change is:

answer.text: Not a material change; only a change within the same methodology is material
A material change significantly influencing investor decisions; the AIF must comply with SEBI disclosure and reporting requirements
Material only if fund-level NAV shifts by more than 15%
Immaterial if the new methodology is IPEV-endorsed

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.12: 'Any change in the valuation methodology or approach shall be construed as a material change significantly influencing the decision of the investor to continue to be invested in the AIF scheme.' Distinct from this, a change in APPROACH WITHIN the same method is NOT material (though it still requires disclosure of both old and new results per Section 11.11 end). The Trap: Options A and D understate materiality; Option C invents a quantitative threshold that doesn't exist for methodology switches. The key is that methodology SWITCH = material, but a parameter tweak WITHIN the same method = not material. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same material-change concept. XIX-A tests it from an LP-exit / opt-out angle. SEBI Mutual Fund regulations have a parallel 'fundamental attribute' change rule. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before authorising a methodology change, get written board-of-trustee approval and a valuer memo justifying the switch (e.g., investee now profitable → switch from revenue multiple to EBITDA multiple is justified). Attach both to the annual PPM change disclosure to SEBI.
